name: Box Filter Residual Analysis
description: Evaluates the residual noise extracted by a linear box filter to detect widespread image smoothing. AI generation models often apply aggressive internal denoising and interpolation steps, leaving behind statistically abnormal smooth textures compared to natural camera sensor noise.
algorithm: Spatial Domain Residual Extraction and Denoising Profiling
mechanism: The algorithm applies a simple spatial box filter (moving average) to the image and subtracts it from the original to isolate the high-frequency residual signal (noise). In authentic images, this residual exhibits characteristic natural sensor noise traits. In AI-synthesized or heavily retouched images, the residual contains 'dead zones' of absolute zero variance where the model applied excessive smoothing, interspersed with structural boundary artifacts.
parameters: Filter Type: 3x3 or 5x5 Box Filter, Operation: Original - Filtered, Analysis: Variance of Residual Noise
accuracy: Moderate to High (75-85%) - Very robust for uncompressed or cleanly compressed images.
source: Fridrich & Kodovsky (2012) on Rich Models for Steganalysis
useCase: Detecting AI-generated digital art, identifying aggressive noise-reduction filters, and recognizing global image smoothing manipulations.

references.title: Fridrich, J. & Kodovsky, J. (2012). Rich Models for Steganalysis of Digital Images. IEEE TIFS.
Gonzalez, R.C. & Woods, R.E. (2018). Digital Image Processing. 4th Edition. Pearson.

strengths:
• Extremely fast and lightweight spatial domain operation computation.
• Leverages established steganalysis techniques (SRM) built for noise extraction.
• Exceptional at identifying non-photorealistic synthetic smoothing and blurring.
• Less affected by semantic content and focused purely on local texture variations.
limitations:
• Accuracy significantly degrades after heavy JPEG compression or aggressive downsampling.
• High ISO (grainy) AI images or post-processed natively added film-grain can easily bypass detection.
• Difficult to differentiate between AI generation and standard modern smartphone denoising filters.
• Requires uncompressed image inputs (e.g., PNG, TIF) for optimal forensic signal preservation.
